headline: Primary Suite Addition: Choosing the Right Contractor
articleBody:
Deciding to add a primary suite is a big step, and picking the right contractor makes all the difference. You want someone who understands the unique challenges of expanding your home, not just any builder. It’s not just about getting the job done; it’s about getting it done right, blending seamlessly with your existing home, and avoiding unexpected headaches.

When you're comparing options, look for contractors with specific experience in home additions. Ask them if they've handled projects where load-bearing walls changed or a new foundation was needed, as these are common with primary suites and require a certain level of expertise. They should be able to clearly detail the project scope and any exclusions, so you know exactly what you’re paying for. Don't be shy about asking for proof of their licensing and insurance; this protects you if anything goes wrong. Always request references for comparable projects—seeing their past work firsthand, or at least hearing about it from previous clients, gives you peace of mind. A good contractor will also have a written change-order process, so there are no surprises if you decide to modify something mid-project. Finally, they should provide realistic schedule assumptions, especially considering factors like permit reviews and material availability, and show how they coordinate inspections and specialty trades like plumbers and electricians.

What to Prepare Before You Start
Before you even call a contractor, think about what you really need and want from your primary suite. Consider your ideal bedroom size, bathroom layout, closet space, and how you envision the new space flowing with your existing home. Having a clear idea of your functional and aesthetic goals will help any contractor provide a more accurate estimate and plan. Also, gather any existing plans for your home if you have them, as this can help speed up the initial assessment phase.
